Question:
Seven students count from \(1\) to \(1000\) as follows:

• Alice says all the numbers, except she skips the middle number in each consecutive group of three numbers. That is, Alice says \(1,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(9,\) \(\ldots,\) \(997,\) \(999,\) \(1000.\)

• Barbara says all of the numbers that Alice doesn’t say, except she also skips the middle number in each consecutive group of three numbers.

• Candice says all of the numbers that neither Alice nor Barbara says, except she also skips the middle number in each consecutive group of three numbers.

• Debbie, Eliza, and Fatima say all of the numbers that none of the students with the first names beginning before theirs in the alphabet say, except each also skips the middle number in each of her consecutive groups of three numbers.

• Finally, George says the only number that no one else says.

What number does George say?
Solution:
Track the numbers left unsaid, since those are exactly the numbers passed to the next student. Each student leaves the second, fifth, eighth, and subsequent corresponding entries of her list.

Suppose the current list begins
\[
a,\ a+d,\ a+2d,\ a+3d,\ldots.
\]
The entries left unsaid begin
\[
a+d,\ a+4d,\ a+7d,\ldots.
\]
Thus the new first entry is \(a+d\), and the new spacing is \(3d\). Starting with first entry \(1\) and spacing \(1\), we obtain the following pairs, each recording the first entry and spacing:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{After Alice:}&\quad (2,3),\\
\text{After Barbara:}&\quad (5,9),\\
\text{After Candice:}&\quad (14,27),\\
\text{After Debbie:}&\quad (41,81),\\
\text{After Eliza:}&\quad (122,243),\\
\text{After Fatima:}&\quad (365,729).
\end{aligned}
\]
The finite list lengths are successively \(1000,333,111,37,12,4,1\). Any incomplete final group here has just one entry, so it contributes no middle entry to the next list.

After Fatima, the remaining numbers would therefore be \(365,1094,\ldots\), but only numbers through \(1000\) are allowed. Exactly one number remains, so George says \(\boxed{365}\), choice C.
